name: Asuri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read the Asuri sketch in Grierson/Konow 1906 Linguistic Survey of India vol. IV (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.38696): no accent/stress statement in the Asuri section.

sources.citation: Khalid, Zoya. 2020. A Phonological Sketch of Asur. Language in India 20(8) [August 2020]: 252-268. ISSN 1930-2940.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 2.1-2.9 cover phoneme inventory, vowels/allophones, diphthongs, consonant clusters, gemination, nasalization, reduplication, syllable structure ((C)V(C), (C)VV, Maximal Onset Principle) and loan-verb adaptation; grep for stress/accent/prosod/suprasegment/pitch/tone gives zero hits. Conclusion (p. 266) lists six 'main features', none prosodic. Data from Bishunpur block, Gumla district.

sources.citation: Khalid, Zoya. 2020. A Grammatical Sketch of Asur: A North Munda language. Proceedings of the 17th International Conference on Natural Language Processing (ICON), pp. 40-49. Patna: NLPAI.
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix B 'Asur Phonology' (pp. 47-48) gives consonant and vowel inventories (citing Khalid 2020 LII), says vowel length and nasalization are not phonemic and intra-syllabic clusters are rare; no mention of stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Baskaran, S. Ganesh. 2015. Consonant Sequence and Syllable Formation in Asuri. Language in India 15(5) [May 2015]. (Not in Glottolog; cited by Khalid 2020.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Syllable types VC, CV, CVC; monosyllabic to pentasyllabic words; defines light (open) vs heavy (closed/diphthongal) syllables in a generic syllable-weight discussion; Fig. 2 is a textbook syllable tree whose 'tone (τ)' node is schematic, not a claim about Asuri.

sources.citation: Baskaran, S. Ganesh. 2015. Phonemes of Asuri. Language in India 15(4) [April 2015]: 59-77. (Not in Glottolog; cited by Khalid 2020.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Describes 5 short + 5 long vowel phonemes (treats length as phonemic, unlike Khalid), consonants with distribution, allophones, diphthongs; the only 'suprasegmental' mention is vowel length ('All segmental monophthongs and suprasegmental length vowels distribution...'). Author at Dept. of Linguistics, Assam University; data from Gumla district.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) [text by Sten Konow]. 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Asuri section pp. 135-140 (Kherwari > Asuri, incl. Brijia).
sources.harvard_location: WID Old Widener 3254.1 F; LIN GEN CoPh 5.40; SAN GEN Ud 0010
sources.note: Asuri section (p. 137) has no accent statement, confirming the earlier scan; its 'Pronunciation' paragraph says only 'The pronunciation mainly agrees with Mundari' (then discusses palatal n, h>w, r, semi-consonants). The Mundari section (p. 85) says 'Accent.—The accent is the same as in Santali', and the Santali section (p. 39) says 'In words of two syllables the accent usually rests on the first... The final syllable is, however, accented when it ends in a semi-consonant, when the last syllable is long and the first short, when the word ends in ii, and when it is a reduplicated or reflexive…

sources.citation: Hahn, Ferdinand. 1900 [Glottolog gives 1901]. A Primer of the Asur dukmā, a dialect of the Kolarian language. Communicated by G. A. Grierson. Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 69(1), no. 2: 149-172 (read December 1899).
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter I 'Transliteration' (p. 153) has only §1 Vowels (sound values by English keywords, with length marked) and §2 'Hiatus and consonants' (the glottal 'check' after vowels); no accent/stress/tone anywhere in the 24-page primer (scanned grep: 0 hits). Speakers of Ranchi, Palamau and Surguja.

sources.citation: Khalid, Zoya (Centre for Endangered Languages, Central University of Jharkhand) — any fuller Asur documentation (dissertation, grammar or dictionary) beyond the two 2020 sketches; existence not confirmed (ACL author page lists only the ICON sketch; Shodhganga search for Asuri/Asur linguistic theses returned none).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Khalid is the only modern field linguist publishing on Asur; her 2020 sketches omit prosody, so a fuller description would be the first place an Asur stress statement could appear.

sources.note: Asuri is mutually intelligible with Mundari (Khalid 2020) and LSI IV says its pronunciation 'mainly agrees with Mundari'; Osada's chapter gives the Mundari stress rule, the closest-relative proxy. Not an Asuri statement.
